verses.text: So let us move on from the first lessons about Christ and grow up. We do not need to lay the foundation again: turning away from actions that lead to death, and trusting God,
teaching about baptisms, laying hands on people, the dead rising to life, and God's judgment that lasts forever.
And we will move on, if God allows it.
Some people once had their eyes opened to the truth. They tasted the gift from heaven and shared in the Holy Spirit.
They tasted how good God's word is, and the powers of the world to come.
If they then turn away, it is impossible to bring them back to turning from sin. They are nailing the Son of God to the cross again for themselves, and shaming him in front of everyone.
Land that drinks in the rain that often falls on it, and grows a good crop for the people who farm it, receives a blessing from God.
But if it grows only thorns and weeds, it is worthless and close to being cursed. In the end it will be burned.
Dear friends, even though we talk like this, we are sure that better things are true of you, things that come with salvation.
God is fair. He will not forget your work and the love you have shown him by helping God's people, and by still helping them.
We want each of you to keep working just as hard to the very end, so that what you hope for will surely happen.
We do not want you to become lazy. Instead, copy those who receive what God promised because of their faith and patience.
When God made his promise to Abraham, there was no one greater for him to swear by, so he swore by himself.
He said, "I will surely bless you, and I will give you many, many descendants."
So Abraham waited patiently, and he received what God promised.
People swear by someone greater than themselves. Their oath proves what they say and ends every argument.
God wanted to show very clearly to those who would receive his promise that his plan would never change. So he backed his promise with an oath.
God cannot lie, and these two things, his promise and his oath, can never change. So we who have run to God for safety can be greatly encouraged to hold on to the hope set in front of us.
This hope is like an anchor for our souls, firm and safe. It goes behind the curtain into the most holy place in heaven,
where Jesus has already gone ahead of us, for us. He has become a High Priest forever, in the line of Melchizedek.
